title: Electronics - Chapter 6: DFT for In-Circuit Test and JTAG

questions.question: When must in-circuit testing capability be designed into the PCB?
options: Only after the first field failure is returned from a customer.
At the layout stage (DFT), not as an afterthought.
Only in the purchasing PO notes, never in copper.
After silk-screen is approved by marketing.
questions.explanation: must be designed into the PCB at the layout stage

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: However, final testing - in-circuit testing capability - must be designed into the PCB at the layout stage.

questions.question: For dense designs, when is it far easier to place test points?
options: After every route is finished and copper is poured.
At placement time, prior to routing.
Only during ICT fixture debug on the production floor.
Never - ICT fixtures invent pads without copper.
questions.explanation: at the time placement, prior to routing

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: With dense designs it is far too difficult to try to wedge test points into a routed bus after the fact.

questions.question: Without JTAG, test engineers commonly require:
options: Zero test points to protect signal integrity always.
At least one test point per net for full testing coverage goals.
Test points only on the company logo net.
That all nets remain completely inaccessible by probe.
questions.explanation: at least one test point per net

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: However, if full testing is required on a PCBA without JTAG, it is very common for test engineers to require at least one test point per net, except for power and GND which should include many test points sprinkled about the PCB for adequate access.

questions.question: Why can adding DFT for ICT get expensive?
options: There are many fixture/process parts and software costs tied to coverage choices.
Test points are free and never affect schedule or BOM cost.
ICT fixtures are always included with Quickie-Cheapo fab quotes.
JTAG eliminates every cost related to manufacturing test.
questions.explanation: DFT for ICT can get expensive

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: There are many factors weighing into the decision of whether to include DFT for ICT into a design layout.

questions.question: Chapter 3/6 alignment - recognize the need for testability means:
options: Ignoring how assemblies will be tested until after release.
Planning bed-of-nails/functional (etc.) approaches with stakeholders early.
Assuming optical inspection replaces ICT fixtures entirely.
Testing only the programming header and skipping in-circuit coverage.

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design

questions.question: True or false: Thinking about DFT only at PCB documentation time is probably too late.
questions.explanation: too late to begin thinking about it at the PCB documentation stage

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: PCB Documentation Finishing the routing, drilling, and design-checking completes only the graphic portion of a design, but there are other aspects of the design which the CAD data cannot address alone.

questions.question: For a sourcing interview, DFT literacy helps you:
options: Claim test is free so piece price can ignore fixture and coverage tradeoffs.
Discuss how layout decisions change ICT/JTAG cost, yield learning, and NPI risk.
Delete test requirements from every RFQ to win on schedule alone.
Treat EMS test capability as unrelated to the bare-board supplier choice.

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
